title: Flutter 3.38.1: App Store Connect rejects iOS archive with invalid LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO
body: After upgrading to Flutter 3.38.1, submitting my iOS archive to App Store Connect fails validation with: “The binary is invalid. The encryption info in the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO load command is either missing or invalid, or the binary is already encrypted. This binary does not seem to have been built with Apple's linker.” This did not happen before the upgrade. I am on macOS 15.6.1 with Xcode 16.3, and flutter doctor reports no issues.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Flutter 3.38.1, App Store Connect rejects my iOS archive because LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO is missing or invalid and says the binary does not appear to have been built with Apple's linker.
N0.label: N0 App Store validation failure reported

symptoms_visible: The same LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO validation error still appears after updating to Flutter 3.38.2 and running flutter clean.
N1_x.label: N1_x update and clean aftermath

symptoms_visible: Both Xcode's Validate App operation and distribution produce the same invalid-encryption-information error.
N2.label: N2 project evidence and validation mode collected

symptoms_visible: The upload still fails with the same App Store validation error for the sqlite3 framework; nothing in my project changed.
N3.label: N3 stale simulator native asset isolated

symptoms_visible: After running flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only immediately before archiving, my archive validates successfully.
An affected user also reports that an archive produced with the fixed main channel validates successfully.
N4.label: N4 workaround and fixed toolchain verified

symptoms_visible: The iOS device archive contains only the native frameworks needed by that build and passes App Store Connect validation without the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO error.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Treat the failure as stale build output that can be resolved by updating Flutter to 3.38.2 and running flutter clean before rebuilding.
solution.concrete_example: Update to Flutter 3.38.2, run flutter clean, rebuild the archive, and submit it again.

edges.comment: The reporter actually updated to Flutter 3.38.2 and ran flutter clean, but the same validation error remained. A generic older Run Script workaround was also tried in the thread without resolving the issue.

question_patterns: Can you share your pubspec.yaml or dependency list?
Does the project depend on sqlite3 or another package that produces native assets?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My pubspec includes sqflite_sqlcipher, sqflite, and an override for sqlite3 version 3.0.1, along with the rest of my dependencies.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This is a newly created counter app with no packages that emit native assets, and build/native_assets/ios is empty.
The project uses a newer sqlite3 release, but it still generates separate device and simulator native frameworks.

question_patterns: Can you share the complete ContentDelivery.log from the failed submission?
What is the complete validation response rather than the shortened dialog text?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here is my ContentDelivery.log. It reports status 409 and says the binary's LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO is missing or invalid and that the binary does not seem to have been built with Apple's linker. Another affected project produces the same message.

question_patterns: Does this happen when you select Validate App, or only while using Distribute App?
Can you run Xcode's Validate App operation on the archive and report the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I originally saw it while distributing. I then tried Validate App directly, and I still get the same errors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Validate App succeeds; the error occurs only after uploading through Distribute App.
Validate App and Distribute App both fail with the same text but different request IDs.

edges.comment: The reporter supplied pubspec.yaml, a full ContentDelivery.log, and later Info.plist, Runner.xcodeproj, and pubspec.lock in a support archive. The screenshot and log from another affected project are folded into the same simulated user side.

solution.intent: Reproduce and inspect the archive to isolate whether a simulator-only sqlite3 native framework is being retained and embedded in a device archive.
solution.concrete_example: Compare a clean device archive with one produced after flutter build ios --simulator. The failing sequence leaves sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework in the device Runner.app/Frameworks directory, while archiving directly after flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only omits it and validates.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the project files and observed validation failures. Engineers reproduced the build sequence and determined that Flutter's xcode_backend embedding step copied the entire shared build/native_assets/ios directory, including sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework left by a simulator build, instead of copying only the assets selected for the current device build.

edges.comment: Engineering reproduction showed that a simulator build followed by a device archive contaminates the archive with sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework. This conclusion is engineer-side analysis, not something the reporter identified from the error message.

question_patterns: Can you run flutter clean followed by flutter build ios --config-only, avoid running a simulator build, then archive and validate in Xcode?
Please test a clean config-only build immediately before archiving and report whether App Store validation succeeds.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: That option works for me. After flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only, I archived in Xcode and validation passed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clean config-only sequence still embeds sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework and validation fails with the same error.
It passes when I also run flutter pub get and pod install before opening Xcode, as long as I do not run the app on a simulator before archiving.

question_patterns: Can an affected user build and validate the app using a Flutter main build containing the native-assets embedding fix?
Does the archive pass validation with the fixed Flutter toolchain?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the fixed main channel and it does the trick; I was able to validate and deploy my app.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The fixed main build still places the simulator sqlite3 framework in the device archive and App Store validation still fails.

edges.comment: The first answer is the original reporter's verification of the clean/config-only workaround. The fixed-main verification came from other affected users and is folded into the simulated user side. Both are handler-initiated build tests, so this edge is clarification_only.

solution.intent: Use a Flutter toolchain containing the native-assets embedding fix so device archives include only frameworks selected for the current build; until then, generate a clean config-only device archive without first running a simulator build.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a Flutter build containing the native-assets fix. Flutter must not copy the entire build/native_assets/ios directory into Runner.app; it should embed only the frameworks required by the current device build. Until that toolchain is available, run flutter clean && flutter build ios --config-only immediately before archiving and do not run a simulator build first.
solution.inference_hint: For the reporter's sqlite3-dependent project, the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO message is a consequence of a simulator-only native framework being included in a device archive. Engineers derived the precise Flutter bug by reproducing the simulator-to-device build sequence and reading xcode_backend.dart. Later comments identified a separate, similar LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO failure affecting apps with an empty native-assets directory; that separate AOT/App.framework issue should not replace the native-assets diagnosis for this reporter.

edges.comment: Flutter fixes for the native-assets case were made available on main. The reporter verified the documented clean/config-only workaround, and affected users verified the corrected main toolchain. Channel scheduling and cherry-pick coordination are intentionally not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the reporter's root cause: a simulator build generated sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework, and Flutter later embedded that stale simulator-only native asset into a device archive because the embedding step copied the whole shared native-assets iOS directory instead of only assets selected for the current build.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the sqlite3 dependency, the failure of both Validate App and distribution, the simulator-then-device reproduction, and inspection of the archived Frameworks directory.

Must recommend using a Flutter toolchain containing the native-assets embedding fix; flutter clean followed by flutter build ios --config-only before archiving, without first running a simulator build, is acceptable as a temporary workaround.
Must not present upgrading to Flutter 3.38.2 plus a generic flutter clean as sufficient, because that exact attempt left the reporter's error unchanged.
Must scope the diagnosis to this project's native-assets frameworks rather than claiming a universal AOT/App.framework defect.
Must require successful archive validation by an affected user before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Flutter application developer with a large dependency graph; comfortable sharing project files, running Flutter and CocoaPods commands, changing SDK versions, and archiving through Xcode, but relies on Flutter maintainers to analyze generated Mach-O frameworks and tool internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and conversational; supplies requested files and exact errors, asks practical questions about Xcode validation, reports attempted workarounds directly, and prefers a real toolchain fix over downgrading.
